subject: Service diversion: EU & APAC cloud region disruption — immediate routing guidance
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <danielle@acme-retail.com>, infra-ops@acme-retail.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 03:12:00 +0000
Subject: Service diversion: EU & APAC cloud region disruption — immediate routing guidance

Hi Danielle / Acme infra team,

Quick update from Redwood: we are seeing a regional provider network fabric issue affecting two of our primary serving clusters (eu-central and apac-sin) that is causing elevated latencies and token-backpressure for requests routed to those clusters. Our telemetry shows increased error rates for requests that prefer eu and apac endpoints starting ~02:45 UTC.

What we recommend right now (immediate steps you can apply server-side / proxy-side):
- Short term: switch traffic for critical reads/writes to the us-west-2 (us) region endpoints listed below. Us-west is healthy and has spare capacity.
  - Hostnames: api.us-west-2.redwood.ai and streaming.us-west-2.redwood.ai
- For EU traffic: failover to eu-west-1 (secondary EU pop) if possible; otherwise route to us-west with prefer-region header removed.
- For APAC traffic: route to sg1 (apac-sg) fallback endpoint: api.apac-sg.redwood.ai. Note: this will increase cross-region egress and you may see slightly higher latency.

We are enabling automatic fallback routing on the Redwood side for customers who use default region routing; however, customers using strict region pinning will need to update their client config or DNS routing to allow the above fallback.

We have attached a short checklist ("traffic-migration-checklist.csv") and a one-page step-by-step PDF for engineers to apply the host overrides quickly. If you want, we can open a dedicated short Zoom and our SREs will walk your infra team through the cutover.

Planned follow-ups from Redwood:
- 03:30 UTC: enable routing fallback and capacity headroom in us-west for impacted tenants (in progress).
- 07:00 UTC: status update with root-cause hypotheses.
- After containment: full post-incident summary and recommended long-term routing controls.

I will keep this thread updated as things progress. Apologies for the disruption — we know this is disruptive to you.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: reroute_instructions_v1.pdf (1 page, PDF), traffic-migration-checklist.csv (CSV, 12 rows)

Danielle — quick technical clarifications:
- apac-sg and us-west hosts share the same authentication boundary; your existing API keys will work without changes. No new certs or tokens required.
- Expected RTT delta: APAC -> us-west typically adds ~120–220 ms median depending on carrier; apac-sg fallback should be ~40–80 ms median for Singapore-hosted clients. We will surface E2E percentiles on the status page.
- Throughput: there is currently spare serving capacity in us-west; we have opened an additional worker pool and increased batching limits to improve throughput for diverted customers. Expect token-per-second capacity to be within ~10% of nominal for most workloads.

Operational guidance (short checklist):
1) If you have region-pin in your client header (x-rw-region), remove or set to "any" so our fallback logic can select a healthy pop.
2) If you rely on DNS overrides, update to the temporary hostnames we shared.
3) Watch for 429 spikes during cutover; if you see sustained 429s, notify us and we'll provision more burst capacity.

I'll be on the call in 5 mins if you want real-time help.

-Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Danielle / Acme infra,

Thanks for the rapid response yesterday. Per Karthik's notes, we've confirmed:
- Your keys work against apac-sg and us-west hosts. No client-side auth changes required.
- We enabled fallback routing for tenants that do not block region changes; this has contained the majority of errors.

Attached are two artifacts for your operations team: reroute_instructions_v1.pdf (step-by-step host override + proxy examples) and traffic-migration-checklist.csv (a short validation list: health-check endpoints, percent of traffic to move, and rollback instructions).

Open items for Acme to action (recommended priority):
- By 14:00 UTC today: confirm you've updated any hardcoded region pin or DNS overrides for your edge proxies.
- If you have a canary cohort: route 10% of traffic to apac-sg first and monitor 95th percentile latency and 5xx rates.
- If you cannot change region pinning: reply and we will run an account-level override for you (RTP temporary).

Our SRE oncall (Karthik) will continue to monitor. Marissa from customer success will coordinate billing/credits if needed.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Danielle Park <danielle@acme-retail.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 18:45:00 +0000
Subject: Post-incident summary: 2025-09-14 EU/APAC routing disruption and next steps

Team / Acme,

Summary: the root cause was a provider-side BGP route flap combined with an internal cache warming bug that amplified backpressure to serving pools in eu-central and apac-sin. The incident window (elevated error/latency) ran from ~02:45 UTC to 09:10 UTC on 2025-09-14. Redwood enabled automatic fallback routing and increased burst capacity in us-west to contain the impact.

Customer impact for Acme Retail: some requests routed to eu/apac experienced latency >2s and intermittent 5xx. Customers using strict region pinning saw higher error rates until region-pin was relaxed. Based on our logs, Acme's production traffic had ~3.7% error-rate spike at peak and stabilized to baseline after failover.

What we did:
- Immediate: activated cross-region routing override and increased worker pool in us-west.
- Short term: provided per-customer host override artifacts and hands-on SRE support.
- Post-incident: triaged cache warm-up logic and deployed a fix to reduce amplification on subsequent route flaps.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Karthik: complete deployment of improved cache-warming throttles by 2025-09-20.
- Neha / Marissa: coordinate any billing credits or contract exceptions for impacted tenants; draft communication to customers by 2025-09-18.
- Product (Laura): evaluate region-pin opt-in / opt-out controls in Console by 2025-10-01.

Requested ask for Acme: please confirm whether you'd like Redwood to keep an account-level fallback override in place for 72 hours, or whether you'll manage the host overrides internally. If you choose the account-level override, we will schedule a follow-up call to walk through the rollback steps.

Thanks again for your partnership — apologies for the disruption. If you want the full event log or raw traces for your compliance team, reply and we'll provide a redacted bundle.

Laura Bennett
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
